plugins.description: Bridge QQ official-bot private chats into DeepSeek Harness agent sessions - same session, same memory, same permissions. No second QQ gateway, no copy-pasted system prompt.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-qqbot-bridge

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.19-339933.svg)](package.json)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-139%20passing-brightgreen.svg)](TEST-REPORT.md)
[![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-ff69b4.svg)](#contributing)

> Route QQ private messages into the AI team sessions you **already** have in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — same session id, same memory, same permissions. No second QQ gateway, no copy-pasted system prompt.

![Asking the 程序员 Bot for a quicksort on QQ, and getting the real session's answer back](assets/demo.gif)

*Real run: a private message on QQ, answered by the Bot's actual DSH session — code, files and all. The same conversation is waiting in the DSH Web UI.*

```
        QQ app                          ┌─ DSH Web UI ─┐
           │                            │  程序员 chat  │
    private message                     └──────▲───────┘
           ▼                                   │  the same session
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
   │  dsh-qqbot-bridge  →  the Bot's REAL session (history + memory + ...) │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## The problem

You already run a **team of agents** inside DSH: several Bots, each with its own long-lived
session, its own role instructions, its own long-term memory, its own tools and workspace.
You want to talk to them **from QQ**.

The obvious approach — *"write a QQ bot that calls the model with the same system prompt"* —
silently throws away everything that made the team worth building: the conversation history,
the memory files, the permissions, the workspace, the resume-after-restart behaviour.
You end up with a stranger wearing the same name.

This project does not do that. It **delivers a QQ message into the session that Bot already
has**, and relays the Bot's answer back to QQ.

## What makes it different

| | Typical QQ ⇄ LLM bridge | **dsh-qqbot-bridge** |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Copies the system prompt | **Reuses the real session** — `sessionController.resolveAgent(sessionId)` then `agent.followup(createUserMessage({ source }))` |
| Context | Starts from scratch | The Bot's actual history, memory, tools and workspace |
| Web ⇄ QQ | Two disconnected worlds | **One session**: start on QQ, continue in the Web UI, same context |
| QQ gateway | Opens its own connection | **Borrows** the one the official plugin already runs — no second login, no credential race |
| Allowlist | `[]` often means *everyone* | `[]` means **nobody** (fail-closed); refused peers are only *recorded*, never auto-granted |
| Observability | Silence when it breaks | Console lines **and** `bridge-status.json` — "did it load?" always has an answer |
| Official commands | Frequently swallowed | `/bot-ping`, `/bot-status`, … keep working |
| Long conversations | Pins one session id | Re-reads `state.json` before every send, so a session that rolls over to a new part keeps working |
| Group chats | Often on by default | Off, and group traffic is handed back to the stock chain untouched |

Every row above is backed by a test or a real run log — see [`TEST-REPORT.md`](TEST-REPORT.md).

## How it works

```
QQ private message
      │
      ▼
@tencent-connect/dsh-qqbot   (stock plugin + a tiny local fork, patch 0001)
      │   owns the only QQ websocket, holds the credentials
      │   publishes: ctx.provide('qqbot', { setMessagePreHandler, sender, replyTargetFor, … })
      ▼
dsh-qqbot-bridge   (this project — consumes the service, never opens a socket)
      │   1. allowlist gate      (empty ⇒ refuse everyone, record the OpenID only)
      │   2. command router      /管家 /设计师 /程序员 /聊天 /团队 /当前   → routing.json
      │   3. per-OpenID FIFO queue + message-id de-duplication
      │   4. read state.json (READ-ONLY) for that Bot's CURRENT session id
      │   5. sessionController.resolveAgent(sessionId) → agent.followup(msg)
      ▼
the Bot's real DSH session          ← the very same one the Web UI shows
      │   msg.source.kind = 'qqbot-bridge'   (so QQ and Web turns are distinguishable)
      ▼
ctx.on('session/event') collects the answer, turn/end closes it
      │
      ▼
back to QQ (chunked, with honest failure and timeout messages)
```

The bridge registers **one** Cordis service of its own (`qqbotBridge`) so an operator can ask
a live host what it is doing.

### Why a fork of the QQ plugin is required

The stock `@tencent-connect/dsh-qqbot` keeps its `QQBot` instance, `SessionManager` and
outbound sender inside local variables and **registers no Cordis service at all**, so an
external plugin cannot send on the same connection, cannot intercept the middleware chain,
and cannot learn which OpenID a message came from. Starting a second gateway with the same
AppID would race the first one for the event stream.

So the only clean option is a **minimal local fork**, and patch 0001 adds exactly two things:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dist/gateway/middleware-setup.js` | one optional `preHandlers` argument, inserted at the **front** of the middleware chain |
| `dist/gateway/bootstrap.js` | `ctx.provide('qqbot', { setMessagePreHandler, sender, replyTargetFor, manager })` |

No existing statement is modified, and a host that never calls the extension point behaves
exactly as before. Rollback is one dependency range in the profile manifest.
Full evidence in [`patches/0001-qqbot-extension-point.md`](patches/0001-qqbot-extension-point.md).

## Quick start

Prerequisites: DSH with the Web profile, the stock QQ plugin installed and already bound to
your AppID, and DS Bot with your team created.

```bash
# 1. self-check (zero runtime dependencies — no install needed)
node scripts/run-tests.mjs
node scripts/audit-constraints.mjs
node scripts/verify-host-resolution.mjs

# 2. generate the local fork (finds the installed stock package automatically,
#    or pass --from <dir>)
node scripts/make-bridged-qqbot.mjs --out ../dsh-bridged-qqbot
(cd ../dsh-bridged-qqbot && pnpm install --prefer-offline)   # pnpm does not do this for linked packages

# 3. point your Web profile at the fork and mount this bridge (see the diff first)
node scripts/install-profile.mjs --fork ../dsh-bridged-qqbot --project . --dry-run
node scripts/install-profile.mjs --fork ../dsh-bridged-qqbot --project .

# 4. stop dsh, then install inside the profile
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && pnpm install

# 5. start dsh again. You should see the bridge announce itself:
#    [qqbot-bridge] apply() entered (plugin v0.1.0)
#    [qqbot-bridge] allowOpenIds: 0 configured -- FAIL CLOSED, every QQ peer is refused
#    [qqbot-bridge] provided the "qqbotBridge" service
#    [qqbot-bridge] STARTED: transport=dsh-qqbot-bridge/qq | snapshot=...
```

Then allowlist yourself:

```bash
# send any private message to the bot on QQ (it will be refused, on purpose), then:
node scripts/show-openids.mjs          # prints the OpenID that was recorded
# put it into ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml -> allowOpenIds: ["YOUR_OPENID"]
```

Editing `cordis.patch.yml` is picked up by DSH's config hot reload — **no restart needed**.

## Using it from QQ

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/管家` `/设计师` `/程序员` `/聊天` | switch which Bot you are talking to (persisted per OpenID) |
| `/团队` | list the team |
| `/当前` | show who you are talking to |
| anything else | delivered to the current Bot; its answer comes back to QQ |

## Configuration

All of it lives in **your** profile patch, never in this repository:

```yaml
- id: qqbot-bridge
  config:
    allowOpenIds: []        # EMPTY MEANS NOBODY. Add only your own OpenID.
    defaultBot: 管家         # who receives a message from a peer with no switch yet
    allowGroups: false      # v1 is private chats only
    replyTimeoutMs: 600000  # how long to wait for a Bot turn before telling the user
    queueMax: 4             # per-peer queued messages
    textChunkLimit: 4500    # max characters per QQ message
    debug: false
    # statePath / da

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 插件：把输入框模型选择器改成按来源渠道分块 + 下钻选模型，保留搜索与推理强度
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-model-block-picker

[English](README.en.md) | 中文

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 插件 —— **按模型来源分块**的输入框模型选择器。

把官方那个「所有模型拉成一条长列表」的选择器，换成**先按来源渠道分块、再下钻进块内选模型**的两级结构；搜索、推理强度（Reasoning Effort）、模型可用性等原有能力**完全保留**。

---

## 效果

点击输入框右下角的模型位，弹出的不再是长长的平铺列表，而是**按来源分块的卡片网格**：

![分块面板与搜索、推理强度](docs/screenshot-panel.png)

- **① 全局搜索** —— 直接在顶部输入 `v3` / `sonnet` / `r1`，跨全部 17 个来源聚合匹配；回车选中首项。
- **② 按来源分块** —— 每个渠道一张卡片，标出「N 个模型」与「进入 →」。
- **③「当前」标记** —— 正在使用的来源高亮描边 + 右上角黑标。
- **④ 推理强度** —— 当前模型支持 reasoning 时，浮层底部保留 Reasoning Effort 选择器。

触发按钮本身与同排的截图 / 麦克风图标保持同一设计语言（黑底 + 主题 off-white 描边与文字）：

![输入框模型位与同排图标](docs/screenshot-composer.png)

---

## 功能

- **按来源分块**：DeepSeek 账号、DeepSeek API，以及 CodeBuddy / Qoder / TRAE 等第三方渠道，各自成为一张卡片；卡片上显示来源名、模型数量，当前所用来源带「当前」标记。
- **两级下钻**：点卡片 → 进入该渠道内只含它自己模型的列表；顶部 `← 所有来源` 或 `Esc` 返回。
- **全局搜索**：直接输入 `v3` / `sonnet` / `r1` 等关键词即可跨所有来源聚合匹配，回车选中首项；清空即回到分块视图。
- **推理强度保留**：当前模型支持 reasoning 时，浮层底部出现强度选择器（默认 / low / medium / high…）。
- **主题自适应**：浅色、深色均用 DSH 主题 token；深色下触发按钮为黑底 + 主题 off-white 描边/文字，与同排麦克风、截图图标同一设计语言。

## 安装

### 从本机目录安装（开发 / 自用）

在 DSH 会话里对 Agent 说：

> 帮我安装位于 `<本仓库路径>` 的插件

Agent 会执行 `plugin_manager(action: 'install_bundle', target: '<绝对路径>')`。

安装后**彻底退出 DSH 桌面端再重新打开**（客户端 bundle 有启动基线缓存，仅刷新页面不一定加载新代码）。

卸载：`plugin_manager(action: 'remove_bundle', target: 'dsh-model-block-picker')`，回退到官方原生选择器。

## 它是怎么工作的

### 1. 覆盖官方选择器（Slot 影射）

输入框模型位是 DSH 公开的一个**命名插槽**：`conversation.input.model`（`kind: "single"`，会话作用域）。

- 官方实现注册在优先级 `-10`；
- 动态安装的插件注册同名插槽时，系统分配**更低的数值即更高优先级**获胜；
- 本插件显式注册 `priority: -20`，因此作为 winner 覆盖原生组件，卸载即自动回退。

> 注意：`single` 槽位要求同优先级唯一，所以必须用负数优先级，否则会抛
> `single slot already has a registration`。

### 2. 复用官方数据服务（不重复造轮子）

不自己请求后端。通过 `ctx.modelDirectories`：

```js
const directory = models.directoryFor(sessionId);
directory.store   // 快照：{ groups: [{ id, name, models: [...] }], current: { provider, model, reasoningEffort } }
directory.load()  // 拉取目录
directory.select({ provider, model, reasoningEffort })  // 提交选择
```

与 `/model` 命令弹窗**共用同一份会话级目录**，任一入口的切换另一入口立即可见。

### 3. 深色外观的白，来自主题而不是硬编码

早期版本手写 `#1c1f23` 之类的兜底色，在深色下不会反转，导致字和箭头变深灰。现在全部改用真实 token：

| 用途 | token | 深色取值 |
|---|---|---|
| 主文本 | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` | `#f9fafb`（off-white，非纯白） |
| 边框 | `--dsw-alias-border-l1` | `#ffffff0f` |
| 背景 | `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-1/2`、`--dsw-alias-bg-overlay` | — |
| 品牌色 | `--dsw-alias-brand-primary` | — |

深色下额外用 `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` 把触发按钮设为 `.5px` 描边 + 该 token，与右侧截图插件
（`color: var(--dsw-alias-label-primary)` + `fill:none stroke=currentColor stroke-width=1`）
保持同一笔画重量。

> **踩坑记录**：写 CSS 时**别凭印象编变量名**。DSH 里**不存在**
> `--dsw-alias-text-regular`、`--dsw-alias-border-subtle`、`--dsw-alias-surface-overlay`、
> `--dsw-alias-primary` 这些名字——它们会静默回落到你写的兜底值，浅色看着没事、深色就崩。
> 可用 `cordis_inspect_query(platform: 'client', provider: 'Theme', method: 'listTokens')` 查真实 token。

## 文件结构

```
dsh-model-block-picker/
├── package.json          # 清单：dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client 声明
├── cordis.patch.yml      # Loader patch：把本包插进 profile 名单
├── index.js              # 宿主半边（挂 /diag 诊断路由）
├── client.js             # 浏览器半边：React 组件 + 样式 + 插槽注册
├── LICENSE
└── README.md
```

## 诊断

排障时会用到：

- 宿主侧日志前缀 `[dsh-model-block-picker]`（DSH 日志里搜这个）。
- 浏览器端各生命周期节点会打到 `/plugins/dsh-model-block-picker/diag`：
  `module-evaluated` → `apply-called` → `slot-inject-triggered` → `registered-success`。
  若停在 `register-error`，说明槽位/优先级冲突；停在 `apply-error` 多半是 `inject` 未声明就访问了服务。

> **另一个坑**：客户端沙箱对服务访问有白名单。顶层 `inject` 声明了 `['slots','modelDirectories']`，
> 就**不能**再直接读 `ctx.sessions`，否则抛 `service "sessions" is not declared` 并当场崩溃。

## 已知限制

- 只替换输入框（composer）的模型位；`/model` 命令弹窗仍是官方样式（两者共用同一份数据，切换互通）。
- 已寻址的 subagent 会话不提供模型选择（沿用官方约定）。
- 来源分组顺序：DeepSeek 账号 → DeepSeek 官方 → 其余按名称排；如需自定义顺序改 `client.js` 里的分组排序逻辑。

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: Unofficial responsive remote Web UI bundle for DeepSeek Harness with native Desktop isolation.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Community Web UI · Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control English | [中文](README.zh.md) GitHub Release tarballs ship prebuilt `lib/` files and do not run a consumer-side build lifecycle. Source checkouts use `pnpm run build`.

   

Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Instant QR Pairing · Cross-Device PC Access · Mobile Touch Gestures · Cloudflare Tunnels · Secure Device Session

> Seamless remote access for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and desktop client sharing the **exact same interface**: pair an iPhone, Android smartphone, tablet, or another computer from the QR code next to settings. Both ends run the authentic official Web GUI — phones receive an injected portrait touch layer while remote computers enjoy the complete desktop workbench. Access is guarded by expiring pairing tokens and revocable sessions. Built-in LAN binding and optional Cloudflare quick tunnels enable effortless external access with persistent hostnames. This is an **unofficial community plugin** derived from `dsh-web` v0.4.5. It is structured as a cordis bundle: the host half manages pairing tokens, device sessions, `/api/pair` routes, the gated `/remote` channel, and LAN binding; the browser half renders the remote access trigger, QR pairing modal, live device roster, settings card, and mobile portrait touch adaptation. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek. ## What it does - **Entry**: a phone icon beside the settings button in both the expanded sidebar and the narrow rail; its tooltip and accessible label say "Remote access". - **Panel**: "Remote access" title, a "Pair a device" card with the status area ("Waiting for a device" + status badge), a large QR code, the pairing link with its copy button, Stop / Refresh QR actions, and the authorized-device roster (a device name inferred from User-Agent, online/offline, last active time, per-device unpair). Credential-bearing device ids and raw User-Agent values are never rendered. Both the phone and the PC use the same time-limited link: until it expires or the QR is refreshed, that link can pair several devices, each with its own device session. - **Phone side**: scanning the QR binds the phone with a time-limited token and reloads into the **official Web GUI** — there is no second interface to drift from. On touch phones, the plugin injects a responsive adaptation layer over the running UI for portrait and constrained landscape layouts (see "The mobile adaptation layer" below). The accept chain is cookieless (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`): the plugin itself serves the official shell, so the phone needs no harness browser-auth cookie at all. A reopen service worker (https origins) then owns later navigations to `/` from history, bookmarks, or tab restore, so the phone reopens straight into the app instead of a 401 dead end (see Security model). - **PC side**: the same link opens the full desktop Web GUI on another computer over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see a guided blocking page (with a manual pair-token input) and no workspace data behind it. - **Security**: one active token at a time (a refresh invalidates the old link; the link stays re-usable within its expiry window so a scan handed between browsers can complete pairing; it expires). 停止 revokes every paired device and the current token — the `/remote` channel cuts them off on their next request. Pairing is this plugin's access control for the `/remote` channel; direct `/api` on a LAN-exposed bind is governed by the harness fence + browser auth (see Security model). Loopback (127.0.0.1) keeps using `/api` directly, and so does a page an application on this machine delivered — the desktop shell's `dsh-app://app/` or a `file:` page — because a pairing link is reachable only over the network. A paired device is a **full-control credential** (see Security model). - **LAN bind toggle**: the settings card writes a managed block into the profile `cordis.patch.yml` that pins the webserver bind to `0.0.0.0` (on) or `127.0.0.1` (off) — no `--host` command-line dance; an explicit `--host`/`--port` flag still wins. It maintains the matching host firewall rule (Windows Defender via netsh; Linux firewalld/ufw/iptables; other platforms report the firewall as unmanaged) and shows the live bind, the reachable LAN URLs, and the firewall state. - **Live status**: the desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; an `/api` posture probe reports any host whose `/api` fence the SDK leaves open, and the auto-tunnel state appears on the panel while the tunnel is starting. - **Self-update lives next door**: the one-click family update is its own plugin (`dsh-update`, the same sidebar foot seat), so turning remote access off — or disabling this plugin — never removes the update trigger. - **Desktop foot row**: on the wide sidebar the footer-action occupants share the official Settings trigger's line instead of stacking above it, so no single control owns a full-width row; any other foot block (the usage glance card, another plugin's) keeps a full row above them, and the 56px rail keeps the shell's stacked foot. ## The mobile adaptation layer The official desktop layout already auto-collapses the sidebar below 1024px. On top of that, while the viewport is portrait + coarse pointer + narrower than 1100px the plugin injects: - a CSS sheet keyed on CSS-Modules **semantic suffixes** (`[class$="_composerSeat"]`) so the selectors survive official rebuilds that only change hashes: 44px touch targets on the collapsed rail, 16px inputs (prevents iOS focus zoom), safe-area padding for the composer, compact type for the message list and sidebar, a column layout for the settings modal, and a full-width PlanReview card; - a **draggable whale button** as the entry to the collapsed sidebar (position persisted; wired to the official `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`), hidden while the sidebar is expanded; - **gestures**: left-swipe collapses the sidebar, right-swipe in the conversation opens it; long-pressing a session row opens the same action menu as the desktop ellipsis; tapping a session row or anywhere outside the sidebar collapses it again; - **input behavior for touch**: Enter only inserts a newline (send goes through the send button), programmatic composer focus is suppressed (no spurious keyboards), and official tooltip bubbles are hidden because taps leave them stuck; - **mobile plugin scope**: while the layer is active, the right-hand details column and the desktop-oriented tool surfaces (SSH terminal, skill explorer, task board, git graph, pet, usage) are hidden - keyed on the L2 semantic roots (`data-dsh-plugin`), so ownership stays with the declaring plugin and class churn cannot resurrect them. These are render suppressions; the client bundles still load. Activation also closes the details panel through the official `ctx.layout.closeDetails()`. - a **manual opt-out**: `sessionStorage.dsh-remote-force-desktop = 1` disables the whole layer; touch-phone portrait and constrained landscape layouts are adapted, while the native Desktop app and wide desktop-browser layout stay on the official presentation. The paired remote desktop also runs in **host mode**: on this harness line the "configuration plane is local" behavior is a client-side branch on `connection.isLoopback`, and the channel boot script installs the transport hook (`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost = true`) before any boot entry. Host mode is **server-granted**: the hook is installed only when the device-gated app landing (`/pair-app`) published the grant marker ahead of the boot patch, so a shell served to an unpaired browser — a fence-open deployment — never poses as the machine owner.
